subject.title: Generalize post-timeout compaction completion reconciliation across session state

question: Should OpenClaw promote the existing count-only late-success repair into an authoritative compaction-completion reconciliation boundary, and which session fields should that boundary own?
rationale: The code gap is real, but deciding whether the boundary owns only durable accounting or also token freshness, status outcome metadata, auth-profile rotation, memory-flush state, plugin context-engine notifications, and recovery events is a product/architecture ownership choice.

options.title: Design the boundary first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item and have session-state owners define field ownership plus monotonic/idempotent semantics before implementation.

options.title: Limit to narrow follow-ups
options.body: Keep the count-only repair and handle each stale status, activity, or plugin-context field through focused issues without a shared completion event.

options.title: Declare current behavior sufficient
options.body: Close the broad follow-up if maintainers intentionally want only the shipped count reconciliation and no shared compaction completion boundary.

recommendation.title: Design the boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item and have session-state owners define field ownership plus monotonic/idempotent semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the final precursor fix commit and have the clearest recent history on the session write seam most likely to host this boundary.
